A solid state relay (SSR) is just what it sounds like; an IC that acts like a mechanical relay. They allow you to control high-voltage AC loads from lower voltage DC control circuitry. They accomplish this by using infrared light as the ‘contact,’ a solid-state relay SSR is really just an IR LED and a phototriac sealed up into a little box.

Solid state relays, have several advantages over mechanical relays. One such advantage is that they can be switched by a much lower voltage and at a much lower current than most mechanical relays. Also, because there’s no moving contacts, solid state relays can be switched much faster and for much longer periods without wearing out.
Input voltage: 12VDC, Maximum Output Current: 2A, Maximum Output Voltage: 240VAC
Input Voltage of Control Signal: 0-2.5V (low level state), the relay will be on; 3-5V (high level state), the relay will be off.
DC+: Connected to positive supply voltage (supply power according to relay voltage)
DC-: Connected to negative supply voltage
CH1:Signal triggering terminal of relay module
The meaning of high and low level:

Triggered at high level means a forward voltage exists between signal triggering terminal (CH1) and negative supply voltage. It generally connects positive supply voltage and triggering terminal together. When triggering terminal has positive supply voltage or reaches triggering voltage, the relay will pull in.

While triggered at low level means the voltage between the signal triggering terminal (CH1) and negative supply voltage is 0V, or the voltage at the triggering terminal is lower than positive supply voltage. If it lowers to a triggering voltage, the relay will pull in. It generally connects negative supply voltage and triggering terminal together.

The precision of voltage control, rapid response to voltage changes, and continuous monitoring and feedback in closed-loop control systems ensures the AVR can make constant adjustments to maintain the desired voltage level, ensuring connected equipment receive a stable power supply, minimizing the risk of damage due to voltage fluctuations. The transformer is wound around a donut-shaped ferromagnetic core to create two magnetically coupled coils referred to as a primary coil and a secondary coil. When current flows through the primary, a negative magnetic field is created which drops when the voltage drops to near zero. As the output voltage of the primary coil drops to near zero, the secondary coil’s magnetic field absorbs the current from the primary coil. A self-excited multi-vibrator with NE555 as the core. The power supply charges the capacitor C1 through R2, R3, and R4.
When C1 starts to charge, the pin 2 of NE555 is still in Low level, so pin 3 of the output is high,
when the power is charged to C1 to 2/3 power supply voltage through R2, R3, R4, the level of pin 3 of the output changes from high to low,
and the internal discharge tube of NE555 is turned on , The capacitor C1 is discharged through the 7 pins of R4, R3,
NE555, until the voltage across C1 is lower than 1/3 of the power supply voltage,
the level of 3 pins of NE555 changes from low level to high level again. C1 charges again, Such a cycle forms an oscillation.
The charging time is: 0.695(R2+R3+R4)C1, the discharging time is: 0.695(R4+R3)C1,
the output frequency of the oscillator can be controlled by adjusting R4,
the clock oscillation signal of NE555 is continuously added to the 14 feet of CD4017,
Ten LEDs are connected to the 10 output terminals of the CD4017.
When the 10 output terminals of the CD4017 alternately generate high levels under the action of the clock signal,
D1–D10 are turned on in sequence, thereby forming a running light effect.
Adjust the R4 to adjust the flow speed of the LED light.

blocks.text: Tip122 5A 100V NPN Darlington Power Transistor TO-220

The TIP122 is a monolithic NPN Darlington power transistor housed in a TO-220AB package, engineered to deliver high current amplification in a compact, medium-power format. Internally, it consists of two NPN transistor stages fabricated on a single silicon die using planar “base-island” technology, which ensures tight coupling between elements and minimizes parasitic resistance. A pair of integrated base-emitter resistors provides a defined bias path that accelerates turn-off and prevents latch-up, giving the device fast switching characteristics despite its high gain topology.

Thermal management is achieved by bonding the die directly to the metal mounting tab of the TO-220AB package, allowing efficient heat transfer to an external heatsink. The package’s exposed backplate serves as the collector terminal, while its three leads provide connections for base, emitter, and an auxiliary collector pin that helps evenly distribute current and heat under heavy load. This design supports robust operation over a broad junction temperature range (–65 °C to +150 °C), making the TIP122 suitable for demanding power amplification and switching tasks.

Although optimized for ease of use in amplifier and low-speed switching circuits, the TIP122’s Darlington configuration yields exceptionally high DC current gain (on the order of thousands) while maintaining a relatively low saturation voltage. This combination of high gain and low on-voltage drop allows designers to achieve substantial current boosting with minimal drive power and reduced thermal stress on switching elements.

This adapter combines a standard 5.5×2.1mm female barrel jack with a 2-pin screw terminal block, making it easy to connect bare wires directly to devices or boards that require a DC barrel connection. Instead of soldering wires or using complicated connector assemblies, you can simply insert the wire into the screw terminal side and tighten it securely with a small screwdriver.

The screw terminal side is clearly intended for positive and negative wire connection, which helps simplify installation and reduce wiring mistakes. This makes the adapter especially useful in CCTV camera setups, surveillance systems, LED strip installations, prototype electronics, DC-powered modules, and low-voltage bench applications.

If you need to connect a battery pack, DC adapter, power distribution line, or wired power source to a board or module that uses a DC jack, this connector offers a clean and efficient solution. One of the biggest advantages of this adapter is that it eliminates the need for electrical tape, wire splicing, crimping tools, or soldering, saving time during installation while still providing a secure and stable connection. Its compact shape and professional appearance make it suitable for both field installations and workshop use.

The 5.5×2.1mm female DC power jack adapter is widely used in CCTV camera power wiring because this connector size is one of the most common standards in security systems and low-voltage electronics. It can also be used in breadboard power experiments, DIY electronics, routers, LED drivers, access control devices, and many other DC-powered systems requiring quick terminal-based connection.

Whether you are installing a security camera, building a custom power cable, or creating a simple power input adapter for an electronics project, this connector is a convenient, reusable, and dependable choice.

blocks.text: Knife Tip T12-XS-K RELIFE For Station

The T12-XS-K is a knife-profile soldering tip from RELIFE designed for use with a compatible soldering station. The K-style edge makes it a versatile everyday tool: you can drag-solder fine-pitch ICs, wick and reflow bridges, tin wires, lift pads gently during rework, and run long seams on connectors and shields—all with one tip by simply changing the angle you present to the joint.
✅ One tip, many jobs — the knife edge can act like a fine point, a small chisel, or a mini spreader depending on the angle.
🎯 Drag-solder control — the edge carries a small bead of solder along QFP/QFN leads for fast, consistent results.
🧼 Bridge cleanup — slide the edge across pins with wick/flux to clear solder bridges neatly.
🔧 Pad work — lift or re-tack small pads and jumpers with better visibility than a conical tip.
🔗 Wire & shield seams — run the flat along connector shells and braid for smooth tinning.
🧩 T12 family geometry — recognizable XS-K knife shape for users who standardize their bench on K-style tips.
✅ Fine-pitch IC assembly — drag-soldering 0.5–0.8 mm lead pitch with flux assist.
✅ Rework & repair — cleaning bridges, re-tinning connectors, pad touch-ups.
✅ Wires & jumpers — fast tinning and tack-soldering of small leads.
✅ Shield cans & ground tabs — controlled heat delivery along edges.
✅ Angle = function — use the very corner for pinpoint joints; roll slightly to use the flat for wicking or seam work.
✅ Flux is your friend — pre-flux pads/pins to improve wetting and reduce required dwell time.
✅ Drag-soldering — pre-load a small bead on the edge, touch the lead row, and pull in one smooth motion.
✅ Bridge removal — lay braid on the bridge, set the knife flat, heat briefly, lift straight up.
✅ Pad lift prevention — keep dwell short; if a joint resists, add flux and re-approach rather than pushing harder.
✅ Tip care — keep a thin tin layer on the edge; clean with brass wool rather than a wet sponge to minimize thermal shock.
🧯 Temperature discipline — use the lowest temperature that achieves quick wetting; avoid extended idle at peak heat.
🧼 Between joints — wipe lightly in brass wool and re-tin; a shiny film protects the edge.
🔍 Inspect often — oxidation shows as dull/dry appearance; re-tin with fresh solder ASAP.
🔒 Storage — always leave the tip tinned when parking or powering down.
🧪 Consumable — tips are wear items; replace when the edge rounds off or plating is compromised.
